subject: Node mapping & capacity pre-check — Auraborough (late-stage)
messages:
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Logan Wright <logan_wright@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-09-14T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Auraborough — capacity ask and sizing outline

Team,

Auraborough has moved to late-stage legal and is expecting an M8 pilot signature within the next 10 business days. They confirmed the model footprint and peak QPS we discussed in the call last week. Key numbers (from their tech brief attached):
- Model: custom 40B-ish foundation model (fp16), approx 55GB KV + 20GB weights working set per replica
- Expected steady-state qps: 120 rps
- Concurrency target: 40 concurrent requests at p95 latency target < 600ms
- Average generation: ~600 tokens per request during peak

Request: can you run a node-mapping and availability pre-check across us-west/us-east with an eye to:
1) candidate pool of single-tenant nodes that meet memory/throughput (A100-80 / H100-80 equivalency)
2) delta vs. our normal shared capacity (i.e., how many nodes would be pulled out of shared pool)
3) operational impacts (canary path, rollback plan, fallback variant with quantized model)

I've attached the Auraborough requirements PDF. Please treat this as a soft-hold ask only — we are not committing billing until signatures, but need to avoid a capacity gap if they sign.

Thanks,
Karthik
Director, Strategic Accounts
From: Logan Wright <logan_wright@redwood.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-09-15T10:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Auraborough — capacity ask and sizing outline

Karthik — thanks for the brief. A couple of assumptions that will guide ops' mapping:
- We'll assume model ≈ 75GB working set with KV pinned in GPU memory for latency; plan for 1x hot alloc per replica.
- Target of 20 replicas for redundancy and autoscale headroom (this is conservative; ops may suggest 12–16 depending on batching).
- Prefer us-west primary, failover to us-east for SLA.

Marissa / Stephanie: can you run a quick inventory of available candidate nodes and produce a small node-mapping CSV showing: node SKU, region, #instances available, expected ru/day impact, and whether it can be isolated as single-tenant? If we can get a proposed soft-commit window (preferred: 10 business days), that'll let Sales/Legal align with finance.

Also note: if we need to propose a fallback quantized variant (8-bit) we should precompute perf delta — include perf numbers in the mapping.

— Logan
Head of Capacity Planning
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Logan Wright <logan_wright@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-09-16T15:20:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Auraborough — capacity ask and sizing outline

Attached: node_mapping_proposal_20260916.csv (summary below).

Summary of ops availability (checked against current Dedicated pool and near-term provisioning runway):
- Candidate pool (single-tenant eligible): 14 A100-80 equiv nodes in us-west-2; 6 H100 equiv nodes in us-east-1 (after accounting for existing reservations).
- Estimated replicas supported (comfortably): 12 full-memory replicas in us-west (with careful KV packing), 4 in us-east as failover.
- Shared-pool delta: this would remove ~18 A100-equivalent nodes from shared; projected unit-cost uplift ~18% for the quarter if we hold these on standby (soft hold = reserve but not billed).
- Hold recommendation: 10 business days soft-commit window, with automatic release on signature miss + 72h notice. Ops can implement a tagged soft-hold that prevents autoscaler reclamation but allows preemption on critical infra events.

Notes on fallback: we profiled an 8-bit quantized variant (weights-only quantization) — expected latency improvement ~12% and memory drop ~30% at 1–2% quality degradation (customer must sign off separately). Addendum in CSV includes perf numbers.

Action items:
- Sales: confirm desired hold window and whether single-tenant is required vs. shared-dedicated.
- Legal/Finance: indicate expected PO timeline so we can stretch/shorten hold window.

-Marissa
Capacity Operations
From: Logan Wright <logan_wright@redwood.com>
To: DevOps Lead <ops@auraborough.com>, CFO <finance@auraborough.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>

No billing until signature; this is to avoid a provisioning gap.

Key decision needed from Auraborough: single-tenant (preferred by your performance team) or shared-dedicated with tenancy isolation? Single-tenant has higher cost and longer provisioning lead time.

- We prefer single-tenant nodes for this initial pilot (latency consistency is a hard requirement).
